summary: An 80-foot Wisconsin standard fire tower built in 1932 in Douglas County, staffed as late as 1950 and still standing; its post-2015 fate and public access are not in the sources.

facts.design: 80-foot Wisconsin standard tower with an external protected ladder
facts.agency: Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources (per the National Historic Lookout Register); Central US Lookouts places the site in the Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest

events.note: Register gives 1932 as the build year
Photo caption places a fire guard at Brule Tower in 1950
Statewide plan, announced December 2015, to stop using the DNR lookout towers after an early-2015 assessment of 72; the sources found do not name Brule

evidence.supports: DNR announced plans to stop using its lookout towers, December 2015
evidence.quote: The Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources announced plans Wednesday to discontinue using the fire lookout towers it has scattered throughout the state

evidence.supports: 80-foot Wisconsin standard tower with external protected ladder, built 1932
evidence.quote: This 80-foot Wisconsin standard tower features an external protected ladder and was built in 1932.

evidence.supports: site inside the Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest
evidence.quote: Wisconsin - Douglas County - Chequamegon - Nicolet National Forest - 46N-10-13

evidence.supports: fire guard at Brule Tower in 1950 sighting fire with a firefinder
evidence.quote: Raymond Thompson, Fire Guard at Brule Tower, sighting fire with firefinder, Wisconsin, 1950.

evidence.supports: Osborne Firefinder widely used by Forest Service lookouts through the 20th century
evidence.quote: The Osborne Firefinder was widely used by Forest Service lookouts throughout the 20th century

evidence.supports: firefinder let a lookout pinpoint a fire by sighting its smoke
evidence.quote: This instrument allowed lookouts to accurately pinpoint the geographic location of forest fires by sighting distant smoke through the device.

evidence.supports: assessment of 72 towers still in use to varying degrees in early 2015
evidence.quote: an assessment conducted early this year of 72 lookout towers that are still being used to varying extents

evidence.supports: towers costlier to keep up than useful for spotting fires
evidence.quote: DNR officials determined the towers, built primarily in the 1930s and 1940s, were more costly to repair and maintain than they were useful in spotting fires.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register names the Wisconsin DNR as administrator, while Central US Lookouts places the site inside the Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest. The story reports both and does not settle who holds the land.

sources.title: DNR fires up plans to decommission old lookout towers (UPDATE)

notes_for_editor: Build year 1932 and standing status are consistent across the register and the Forest Fire Lookout Association. Not found: any post-2015 fate, current staffing, or public access information for Brule. The 1950 staffing comes only from a photo caption. The land-manager conflict (DNR vs National Forest) is unresolved; a DNR or Forest Service records check would settle it. No photo URL was available for the 1950 image, so none is listed.
